Category: E-Government
Title: Work Accident

Create a process that helps in gathering information about work accidents (and almost work accidents):

For insured gainful employment, a work accident is considered to be an accident that occurs in the following circumstances, by way of example:

* the accident occurs in a location, at a time and with a cause that correlates to the insured employment
* when working from home
* on the direct route from the permanent place of residence to work, to lunch or on the way home, whereby carpools are also protected
* for training sessions that serve to provide specific professional knowledge, whereby an accident on to way to or from the training centre is considered a work accident
* on the direct route from home, or from the workplace or training centre to a doctor and back, if this interrupts the direct route from the permanent place of residence to work or the route home (the doctor’s visit must be notified to the employer in advance)
* on the way to or from the workplace or training centre with the purpose of taking a child to or collecting them from a childcare facility, a daycare facility, external care or a school, insofar as they have a supervisory responsibility for the child
* when making use of advocacy groups or professional associations (e.g. Chamber of Labour, trade union federation, guild etc.)

For kindergarten children, schoolchildren and students, an accident is considered to be a work accident if, amongst other things

* the accident occurs in a location, at a time and with a cause that correlates to the school or university education or the compulsory kindergarten year that forms the basis of the insurance
* when taking part in a school event or school-related event
* on the direct route from the child’s place of residence or permanent accommodation to kindergarten or a school visit or on the way home
* when performing a practical task prescribed as part of the curriculum and/or the study regulations or
* in certain professional (training) orientations.

In an agricultural or forestry establishment, accidents can be considered work accidents if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment. Depending on the protected group of people, the following tasks are covered by accident insurance:

* working in the household of the owner of the company and/or the employee, if the household serves the company to a considerable extent
* working in connection with providing accommodation for guests
* secondary occupations for the sale of agricultural products from the farm
* working in the context of erecting, converting and repairing buildings that serve the agricultural and forestry establishment
* working in the context of neighbourhood assistance for another agricultural and forestry establishment

Certain accidents are considered the same as work accidents and in many cases can also affect people who do not have accident insurance. Accidents that occur in one of the following situations, among others, are considered to be work accidents outside of professional activity:

* for activities with which services from the Arbeitslosenversicherungsgestez/Arbeitsmarktförderungsgesetz are being made use of (e.g. on the way to an arranged job interview)
* when assisting with an accident or donating blood
* when receiving training, taking part in exercises or serving as a member of one of the following aid organisations:
  * Volunteer fire brigade
  * Volunteer water rescue service
  * Volunteer rescue organisations
  * Austrian Red Cross
  * Austrian Alpine Rescue Service
  * Austrian Water Rescue
  * Austrian Rescue Dog Brigade
  * Avalanche warning committees
  * Air rescue service
  * Radiation detection and survey crews

The employees must inform the employer immediately of:

* any work accident
* any incident that would almost have led to an accident
* any serious and immediate risk to safety and health that they discover
* any defect discovered in protection systems.

The employer must, in turn, immediately report any work accident that leads to
a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate, if it has not been
reported to the emergency services.

Independent of this, every work accident in which a person with accident
insurance has been killed, or injured in such a way that they are unable to
work for three days, in full or in part, must be reported to the responsible
accident insurance provider within five days.

As a self-employed person, please ensure that you not only report accidents
involving people you employ but also those that involve you to the accident
insurance provider in good time.

Students and schoolchildren should report accidents to the competent
directorate. Schools, educational facilities and universities are obliged to
report every work accident through which a person with accident insurance is
physically injured or killed within a maximum of five days to the responsible
accident insurance provider in triplicate.

In the case of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in
writing immediately in line with the conditions and to avoid the provider from
being released from the obligation to perform. If there are fatalities, this
must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been
reported.

### **Process: Reporting and Handling Work Accidents and Near-Misses**

#### **1. Process Overview**
This process governs the reporting, documentation, and escalation of work accidents, near-misses, and safety risks in accordance with legal and insurance requirements. It applies to:
- **Employees** (including those working from home, on business travel, or in training).
- **Self-employed individuals** (reporting accidents involving themselves or employees).
- **Students, schoolchildren, and kindergarten children** (in educational or supervised settings).
- **Volunteers** (e.g., aid organizations, emergency services).
- **Agricultural/forestry workers** (including secondary occupations and neighborhood assistance).

---

#### **2. Process Steps**

##### **2.1. Identification of Work Accidents and Near-Misses**
A work accident or near-miss is defined as an incident occurring under the following conditions (non-exhaustive list):

**For Employees:**
- Occurs during insured employment (time, location, cause related to work).
- While working from home.
- On the direct commute (home ↔ workplace, including carpools).
- During training sessions (including travel to/from training centers).
- On the direct route to/from medical appointments (if pre-approved by employer).
- While transporting children to/from childcare, school, or external care (if supervisory responsibility exists).
- During interactions with advocacy groups (e.g., Chamber of Labour, trade unions).

**For Students/Schoolchildren:**
- Occurs during school/university activities or compulsory education (e.g., practical tasks, school events).
- On the direct route to/from educational facilities.

**For Agricultural/Forestry Workers:**
- Includes secondary occupations (e.g., selling farm products, neighborhood assistance).
- Covers household work for the employer (if significantly related to the business).

**For Volunteers/Aid Organizations:**
- Accidents during training, exercises, or emergency response (e.g., fire brigades, Red Cross).

**Other Covered Incidents:**
- Accidents during job interviews (under unemployment insurance).
- Assisting in accidents or donating blood.
- Participation in aid organization activities (e.g., rescue services).

---

##### **2.2. Immediate Reporting Obligations**
**Employees:**
- **Immediate action:** Report any work accident, near-miss, or serious safety risk to the employer.
- **Serious incidents:** Employers must report fatalities or severe injuries to the **Labour Inspectorate** (if not already reported to emergency services).

**Employers:**
- **Fatalities/Serious Injuries:** Report to Labour Inspectorate **immediately**.
- **Insurance-Reportable Accidents:** Report to the **responsible accident insurance provider** within **5 days** if:
  - The injured party is unable to work for ≥3 days (full or partial).
  - The injured party is insured under accident insurance.

**Self-Employed Individuals:**
- Report accidents involving themselves or employees to the accident insurance provider **without delay**.

**Students/Schoolchildren:**
- Report accidents to the **competent directorate** (e.g., school/university administration).

**Educational Institutions:**
- Report all accidents (injuries/fatalities) to the accident insurance provider **within 5 days** (in triplicate).

**Private Insurance Holders:**
- Report accidents **immediately** (written notice) as per policy terms.
- **Fatalities:** Report within **3 days**, even if previously reported.

---

#### **3. Termination Points**
The process concludes under the following conditions:
1. **No reportable incident:** If no accident, near-miss, or safety risk is identified, the process ends.
2. **Successful reporting:** All required reports (employer, insurance, Labour Inspectorate) are submitted within deadlines.
3. **Non-reportable incident:** If the incident does not meet criteria for a work accident (e.g., unrelated to employment), the process ends after documentation.
4. **Fatality:** If a fatality occurs, the process transitions to legal/insurance claims handling (beyond this process scope).

---
#### **4. Key Terminology**
- **Work Accident:** An accident during insured employment or covered activities (e.g., commute, training).
- **Near-Miss:** An incident with potential for harm but no injury.
- **Serious Injury:** Any injury preventing work for ≥3 days.
- **Labour Inspectorate:** Government body overseeing workplace safety.
- **Accident Insurance Provider:** Entity handling insurance claims for work-related injuries.

---
#### **5. Compliance & Accountability**
- **Employees:** Obliged to report incidents immediately.
- **Employers:** Responsible for reporting to authorities/insurers.
- **Educational Institutions:** Must report student accidents within 5 days.
- **Self-Employed:** Must self-report accidents involving themselves or employees

**Category:** E-Government | **Type:** Administrative & Compliance Process
**Objective:** Ensure systematic reporting, documentation, and follow-up of work accidents (and near-misses) to comply with legal obligations, safeguard insured parties, and prevent future incidents.

### **1. Process Overview**
This process defines the structured steps for reporting, documenting, and escalating work accidents (including near-misses) across different insured groups (employees, students, self-employed, volunteers, etc.). It ensures compliance with regulatory requirements and facilitates timely intervention by relevant authorities (e.g., Labour Inspectorate, accident insurance providers).

- **Employees** (insured gainful employment, students, schoolchildren)
- **Self-employed individuals**
- **Employers** (companies, educational institutions, agricultural/forestry establishments)
- **Volunteer organizations** (fire brigades, rescue services, etc.)
- **Accident insurance providers**
- **Labour Inspectorate**
- **Emergency services**

---

### **2. Process Flow**

#### **2.1 Trigger: Accident or Near-Miss Occurrence**
The process is initiated when:
- A **work accident** occurs (as defined in the legal framework).
- A **near-miss** (incident that *could* have led to an accident) is observed.
- A **serious safety/health risk** is identified.
- A **defect in protection systems** is discovered.

**Termination Point:**
- If the incident does not meet the criteria for a work accident/near-miss (e.g., unrelated to insured activity), the process ends.

**Actions:**
- **Employees/Volunteers:**
  - Report **immediately** to the **employer** (or supervisor) via:
    - Verbal notification (if urgent).
    - Written documentation (e.g., accident report form) as soon as possible.
  - Include details:
    - Time, date, and location of the incident.
    - Description of the accident/near-miss.
    - Injuries sustained (if any).
    - Witnesses involved.

- **Students/Schoolchildren:**
  - Report to the **competent directorate** (e.g., school principal, university administration).
  - Schools/educational institutions must document the incident in their records.

### **Reformulated Process: "Job Application Tracking & Employment Process"**
**Category:** E-Government
**Process Owner:** [Department of Employment Services / Labor Market Administration]
**Process Type:** Citizen-Centric Service Process
**Trigger:** Citizen submits a job application to a company.

---

### **Process Flow**

#### **1. Job Application Submission & Tracking**
- **Input:** Citizen submits a job application to a company via the e-government platform.
- **Action:**
  - The system records the application in the citizen’s **Job Application Log**.
  - The citizen must **regularly report** all job applications submitted (frequency defined by policy, e.g., monthly).
- **Termination Points:**
  - If the citizen **fails to report** applications for [X] consecutive periods, the system issues a **non-compliance warning**.
  - If non-compliance persists, the citizen is **temporarily restricted** from receiving new job offers until compliance is restored.

#### **2. Company Confirmation & Application Rating**
- **Action:**
  - The company **confirms receipt** of the application within [Y] days (e.g., 14 days).
  - The company **rates the application** (e.g., scale: A–E, where A = Strong, E = Weak).
- **Termination Points:**
  - If the company **fails to respond** within [Y] days, the system sends an **automated reminder**.
  - If no response is received after [Z] reminders (e.g., 30 days), the application is **automatically marked as "No Response"** in the citizen’s log.

#### **3. Job Interview Negotiation (If Applicable)**
- **Action:**
  - If the company rates the application **A–C**, they may **initiate an interview**.
  - The citizen and company **negotiate interview terms** (date, format, etc.).
- **Termination Points:**
  - If the company **declines to interview** after rating the application, the process returns to **Step 1** (citizen may apply elsewhere).
  - If the citizen **rejects the interview**, the process ends for this application.

#### **4. Probation Phase (If Hired)**
- **Action:**
  - If the company extends a job offer and the citizen accepts, they enter a **probation period** (duration defined by policy, e.g., 3–6 months).
  - During probation, the citizen works under standard employment terms.
- **Termination Points:**
  - If the company **terminates probation early**, the process returns to **Step 1** (citizen may seek new opportunities).
  - If the citizen **resigns during probation**, the process ends, and they may re-enter the job application cycle.

#### **5. Post-Probation Evaluation & Rating**
- **Action:**
  - After probation, both the **citizen and company** submit **mutual ratings** (e.g., scale: A–E).
  - Ratings are **stored in the system** but **only visible to other job applicants after 1 year**.
- **Termination Points:**
  - If the employment becomes **permanent**, the process ends **unless**:
    - The citizen rates the company **C or lower**, in which case:
      - The citizen **continues receiving job offers** (system flags them as "previously rated poorly").
      - The citizen is **exempt from future reporting obligations** for this company.

#### **6. Permanent Employment (Success Path)**
- **Action:**
  - If the citizen remains employed permanently **and** rates the company **B or higher**, the process concludes.
  - The citizen’s job application log updates to reflect **successful employment history**.

#### **7. Failed Employment (Re-Entry to Job Search)**
- **Action:**
  - If probation ends without permanent employment or if the citizen rates the company **C or lower**, they return to **Step 1** (active job application tracking resumes, but reporting may be waived for this company).

---

### **Key Process Controls & Exceptions**
| **Control Point**               | **Action**                                                                 |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Non-Compliance with Reporting** | Warnings → Temporary restriction on job offers.                           |
| **Company Non-Response**         | Automated reminders → Application marked as "No Response."                |
| **Probation Failure**            | Citizen returns to job search; company may re-rate future applications.   |
| **Mutual Rating Discrepancy**    | System flags for review (e.g., if citizen rates company A but company rates citizen E). |
| **Data Privacy**                 | Company ratings visible to applicants only after **1 year**.               |

---
### **Process Owners & Stakeholders**
- **Primary Owner:** Department of Employment Services (Process Management Unit).

  - **If "No drink" is selected:**

  - **If a drink is selected:**
    - The robot begins preparing the drink.

  - *"Would you like fries or onion wedges? If yes, please select size (Small/Medium/Large)."*

  - **Process Ends.**

       │       │

       │
       └── [Post-Delivery: Feedback/Inventory Check → End]
```

### **Improvements for Clarity & Robustness:**

#### **1. Guest Actions (Food Consumption)**
**Start Event:** *Guest enters the restaurant with hunger*
- **Activity 1:** Guest selects a dish from the menu.

  - **Yes** → Proceed to **Activity 2**.

- **Termination (if guest abandons order):** Process ends for this guest.

---
#### **2. Employee Actions (Order Processing)**
**Start Event:** *Guest approaches employee with order*
- **Activity 1:** Employee records order in **POS system** and collects payment.
  - **Termination (if payment fails):** Process ends; guest leaves.
- **Activity 2:** Employee assigns a **buzzer** to the guest and provides instructions:
  *"Your buzzer will ring when your meal is ready."*
- **Activity 3:** Employee notifies the **chef** of the new order (via digital/verbal communication).
- **Activity 4:** Employee monitors for **meal readiness notification** from the chef.
  - **Gateway (Exclusive):** *Is the meal ready?*
    - **Yes** → **Activity 5**.
    - **No** → **Termination (if order is canceled):** Process ends.

**Activity 5:** Employee activates the guest’s buzzer.
- **Gateway (Exclusive):** *Does the guest respond within 5 minutes?*
  - **Yes** → **Activity 6**.
  - **No** → **Activity 7 (Follow-up)**.

**Activity 6:** Guest collects meal from service hatch; employee hands over the dish.
  - **Termination:** Guest consumes meal (process ends).

**Activity 7 (Follow-up for Non-Responsive Guests):**
- Employee **verbally calls** the guest (repeat up to **2x**).
  - **Gateway (Exclusive):** *Does the guest respond?*
    - **Yes** → Proceed to **Activity 6**.
    - **No** → **Termination:** Meal may be discarded or held for later pickup (manual decision).

**Start Event:** *Chef receives order notification from employee*
- **Activity 1:** Chef prepares the meal.
- **Activity 2:** Chef places the meal in the **service hatch**.
- **Activity 3:** Chef notifies the employee that the meal is ready.
  - **Termination (if order is canceled):** Process ends.

---

1. **Single-Point Guest Interaction:** Guests engage only with **one employee** (order + pickup).
2. **Clear Communication:** Buzzers replace manual calls, reducing kitchen-employee distractions.
3. **Termination Points:** Explicit handling of:
   - Abandoned orders.

1. Guest abandons order.

5. Meal is successfully delivered to the guest.

- **Technology:** Use a **POS-integrated buzzer system** to automate notifications.
- **Training:** Employees should be trained to handle **non-responsive guests** and **order cancellations** efficiently.
- **Feedback Loop:** Add a **guest satisfaction survey** to monitor process effectiveness.

This structured model ensures **clarity, efficiency, and scalability** for high-volume operations.

### **Process: Recourse Management (Subrogation & Recovery)**
**Objective:** Ensure proper handling of insurant recourse cases, including validation, payment requests, dispute resolution, and collection escalation.

### **Process Flow**

#### **1. Trigger: Case Identification**
- **Input:** A claim case is identified where the insurant may be subrogated (i.e., legally required to repay funds).
- **Action:** The clerk retrieves relevant case details (e.g., claim amount, policy terms, legal basis for recourse).

#### **2. Subrogation Feasibility Check**
- **Decision:** Is recourse legally and practically possible?
  - **Yes** → Proceed to **Step 3**.
  - **No** → **Terminate case** (no further action required).

#### **3. Initiate Recourse Request**
- **Action:**
  - Send a formal **payment request** to the insurant, specifying:
    - Amount to be repaid.
    - Legal justification (e.g., fraud, misrepresentation, or policy violation).
    - Deadline for response (e.g., **30 days**).
  - Set an **internal reminder** for follow-up.

#### **4. Monitor Insurant Response**
- **Decision:** Does the insurant respond within the deadline?
  - **Yes** → Proceed to **Step 5**.
  - **No** → Proceed to **Step 7**.

#### **5. Evaluate Insurant’s Response**
- **Decision:** Does the insurant agree to repay?
  - **Agreement** → Proceed to **Step 6**.
  - **Disagreement** → Proceed to **Step 5a**.

##### **5a. Dispute Resolution**
- **Action:** Review the insurant’s reasoning for refusal.
  - **Decision:** Is the insurant’s position valid?
    - **Valid** → **Terminate case** (no further action).
    - **Invalid** → Proceed to **Step 7**.

#### **6. Payment Received**
- **Action:**
  - **Record payment** in the financial system (booking).
  - **Close case** (mark as resolved).

  - Forward the case to a **collection agency** with:

### **Reformulated & Structured Process: "Goods Shipping Process"**
**Process Owner:** Secretary (with support from Logistics Department Head & Warehousemen)
**Scope:** Handling and shipping of goods (both small quantities to end customers and large quantities to retail shops)
**Trigger:** Decision to ship goods (internal or customer request)

---

### **Process Flow**

#### **1. Initiation & Shipping Assignment**
- **Input:** Request to ship goods (quantity specified).
- **Action:** The **secretary** determines the shipping method based on quantity:
  - **Large quantities (≥ threshold, e.g., bulk orders to shops)** → Proceed to **Special Shipping Process** (Step 2).
  - **Small quantities (< threshold, e.g., individual customer orders)** → Proceed to **Standard Shipping Process** (Step 3).
- **Termination Point:** If no shipping is required, process ends.

---

#### **2. Special Shipping Process (Large Quantities)**
**Objective:** Secure logistics provider for bulk shipments.

- **Action 1:** The **secretary** identifies the need for **special shipping** (e.g., freight, palletized, or temperature-controlled).
- **Action 2:** The secretary **invites three logistics companies** to submit offers (RFQ – Request for Quotation).
- **Action 3:** The secretary **evaluates and selects** the most suitable provider based on cost, reliability, and service level.
- **Termination Point:** If no suitable provider is selected, process ends (escalate to management).
- **Output:** Confirmed logistics provider for large shipment.

**Parallel Activity:**
- **Warehousemen** begin **packaging goods** (if not already done) in preparation for pickup.

---

#### **3. Standard Shipping Process (Small Quantities)**
**Objective:** Prepare goods for standard postal/freight shipment.

- **Action 1:** The **secretary** prepares a **package label** (with recipient details, tracking info, and shipping instructions).
- **Action 2:** The **secretary** assesses whether **parcel insurance** is required (e.g., high-value items).
  - If **yes**, the **Logistics Department Head** arranges insurance coverage.
  - If **no**, proceed without insurance.
- **Termination Point:** If labeling/insurance cannot be completed, process ends (escalate to management).
- **Output:** Labeled package (with/without insurance).

**Parallel Activity:**
- **Warehousemen** **package goods** (if not already done) in standard shipping materials (e.g., boxes, bubble wrap).

---

#### **4. Final Preparation & Handover**
**Objective:** Ensure goods are ready for pickup by the logistics provider (special or standard).

- **Action 1:** The **secretary** verifies that:
  - Goods are **fully packaged**.
  - Documentation (label, insurance proof, shipping instructions) is **complete**.
  - Logistics provider (if special shipping) has been **confirmed**.
- **Action 2:** The **warehousemen** stage the goods in the **pickup area** (designated location for logistics providers).
- **Action 3:** The **secretary** notifies the **selected logistics provider** (or postal service for standard shipments) of:
  - Pickup time/window.
  - Location of goods.
  - Any special handling instructions (e.g., fragile, hazardous).
- **Termination Point:** If goods are not ready or pickup fails, process ends (escalate to management).
- **Output:** Goods handed over to logistics provider for delivery.

---
### **Process Endpoints**
1. **Successful Shipping:**
   - Goods are picked up by the logistics provider (special or standard).
   - Shipping confirmation is logged (e.g., tracking number, proof of delivery).
2. **Failed Shipping:**
   - No suitable logistics provider selected (special shipping).
   - Documentation/packaging incomplete (standard shipping).
   - Pickup canceled or delayed.
   - **Escalation:** Notify management for resolution (e.g., re-evaluate shipping method, delay shipment, or cancel order).

---

|                         | - Stage goods in pickup area.                                                         |
